decision: Wire scripts/steward_collect_browser_render.js into the scheduled steward workflow (installing Chromium for it) so the browser-render sensor is evaluated on every run?
whyItMatters: The sensor reports not-evaluated without a fresh browser-render input, so rendered frontend facts stay unobserved on scheduled runs. Adding the step changes the workflow's dependencies and runtime.
evidence: Run locally on 2026-10-28 it rendered 95 pages x 2 viewports in about 4 minutes and found 29 pages with rendered defects the static sensor cannot see.
The collector serves docs/ from a local static server and aborts every external request unsent.
Frontend fixes remain human-gated (CLAUDE.md); this only observes.
recommended: Approve an optional workflow step (npx playwright install chromium; node scripts/steward_collect_browser_render.js --repository $GITHUB_REPOSITORY) that records ok/failed in the existing inputs report.
alternative: Keep it an operator-run collector until a quarter of local runs shows low noise.
